|quote=US states where recreational cannabis is legal have seen a reduction of at least 20% in opioid overdose deaths. […] By comparing overdose death rates before and after legalisation, and between states at different stages of legalisation, the authors of a study published in Economic Inquiry identified a “very robust” causal effect on the reduction in opioid-related mortality. Their econometric analysis puts the fall at between 20% and 35%, with a particularly marked effect on deaths caused by opioids such as fentanyl, the deadliest drug in the United States according to the latest official figures. […] States with legal access to marijuana through dispensaries saw a larger fall in mortality than other states […] The differences could be linked to the growing number of people who self-medicate and “relieve pain by using marijuana and are therefore less likely to become addicted to opioids”.
Some earlier studies had nevertheless reached the opposite conclusion: they found that cannabis use increases the use of opioids obtained without a prescription.
